headline: A controlled robot benchmark reports instruction-grounding declines under scene changes
summary: RoboFollow is an author-designed benchmark intended to test whether embodied policies use language to select a task when the visual scene supports multiple valid actions. Across four controlled scene families, nine evaluated VLA/WAM policies and L0–L3 visual or semantic perturbations, the paper reports sharp declines in selected policies’ Intent Scores—for example, pi0 falls from 98.2% to 0.0% on a Scene 1 layout change, and pi0.5 falls from 100.0% to 34.2% on a Scene 2 combined perturbation. A small pi0.5 robot pilot reports 20/40 successes on training instructions versus 6/40 on a different held-out instruction set, but the comparison is unmatched. These paper-reported results diagnose sensitivity in this short-horizon controlled benchmark; they do not establish general deployment failure rates or broad embodied-agent unreliability.
